changes.before: If count is zero, what happens?
changes.after: Check that an allocation's byte count will fit before multiplying the item count by the item size.

before: size_t is an unsigned size type. Multiplying count by element size can wrap to a smaller value. SIZE_MAX from <stdint.h> is its maximum. For nonzero element size, count > SIZE_MAX / element_size detects an unrepresentable product before multiplication.
This example also rejects zero count as an application policy. A representable byte size is not proof that memory is available; allocation still needs a NULL check.

Expected output or behavior: 7
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain why checking the product only after multiplication is too late. You may trace it without a C compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: size_t is an unsigned type for sizes. A product that is too large can wrap into a small number. SIZE_MAX is the largest size_t value. For a nonzero width, `count > SIZE_MAX / width` checks for a product that would be too large without calculating it first.
This program also chooses to reject zero items. Even a byte count that fits can be too large for available memory, so the malloc result still needs a NULL check.
The count is 3 and the width is one int's size. The checks pass. If allocation succeeds, the program stores 7 in the first item, prints it, and frees the allocation.
Set count to 0. The first check rejects it before multiplication, allocation, or any array access.
